articleTitle: Acoustogyration diffraction of optical waves
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Interaction of acoustic and light waves with accounting for elastooptic and elastogyration effects is theoretically described. Collinear acoustogyration diffraction in quartz and paratellurite crystals is experimentally investigated and thoroughly analysed. Piezogyration effect is experimentally studied for TeO2 crystals. The acoustogyration efficiency and the acoustogyration figure of merit calculated for a number of crystals (GaAs, TeO2 and SiO2) are shown to be too small for experimental detection. On the other side, we demonstrate that the effect of light diffraction on periodical distribution of the imaginary part of dielectric permittivity perturbed through the piezogyration effect can be observed for the case of interaction of optical wave with enantiomorphous ferroelastic domain structure.

articleTitle: Complex modification of the semiconductor laser active area for efficient carriers transport
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In the work, it is proposed iterative model for calculation of spatial-energy carrierspsila distribution in multiple quantum well heterostructure. The model takes into consideration the influence of non-uniform charge distribution on the potential profile. It is discussed the influence of different ways of the structure modification on the carriers transport rate. It is proposed the methodology of complex modification of the geometry of an active area for laser efficiency increase. Some attractive results of the modeling are implemented experimentally both for optically and electrically-pumped structures and have provided record values of the efficiency and output power.

articleTitle: Technique of XeCl-excilamps computer modeling
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The procedure of electric-discharge XeCl-excilamps modeling is presented. There are many reports on the different models of XeCl-excilamps, but for practical applications and theoretical analysis having clear physical sense it is useful to consider a general procedure. In general case program of XeCl-excilamps modeling includes the next subprograms: the subprogram for solution of Boltzmann equation for electrons; subprogram for calculation of solving of set of equations for kinetic processes; subprogram for calculation of solving of set of equations for electric circuit of excitation system; data base for cross-section of reaction with electron participation; data base for rate coefficients of reactions with heavy particles, ions and photons participation. The model must be able to calculate an electrons concentration, density of excimer XeCl* molecules and specific energy deposition in active medium. The knowledge of XeCl* molecules concentration has allowed to evaluate the excilamp output power.

articleTitle: Design of optimization technique for electro- and acousto-optical interactions of light in crystalline materials
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In this paper new approach to the spatial anisotropy 3D-analysis of electro- and acousto-optical effects on the basis of indicative surfaces for different components of tensor describing these effects has been proposed and the optimization technique for such interactions of light with electrical field or acoustical wave in the crystalline materials has been designed. This technique is demonstrated for researched crystals of barium beta-borate, langasite and pure and MgO-doped lithium niobate as prospective acousto- or electro-optic materials.

articleTitle: Band spectrum properties of periodic stuctures, formed by the layers of different materials
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The theory of the band spectrum for the electromagnetic waves propagating in one-dimensional periodic structures formed by two recurring layers of two different materials (dielectric, semiconductor and ferrite) is constructed. The numerical investigations of electromagnetic wave properties are realized. The structures dielectric-dielectric, dielectric-semiconductor, dielectric-semiconductor in a magnetic field, and ferrite-ferrite are considered. It is shown that the dispersion equations for all investigated problems have general outlines. In such case we can compare the structures from the physical point of view. One of the most important properties is the possibility of the band structure control by the external magnetic field. The results of the work show that such materials can be used in practice for the wide spectrum of frequencies from the units of GHz to hundreds of terahertz as filters, mirror coverings, polarization changers, etc.

articleTitle: Observations of instabilities in two-mode He-Ne laser radiation by means of interference of polarized beams
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We studied instabilities in two-mode He-Ne laser generation during half an hour after laser switching-on. We used Wollaston prism, polarizer, collecting lens and microscope in our observations. The pattern observed was a mix of two interference patterns created by the two laser modes. Instability was shown up as alternating appearance of two contrary patterns. Pattern replacement was realized through total pattern disappearance. External stationary magnetic field action appeared to stimulate increase of interference pattern visibility but retained evolution character. Bringing a sufficient delay in one of the interfering beams resulted in qualitative change of interference character. The pattern did not disappear and had a high visibility. Instability was revealed as fringe drift in direction depending on where delay line was put: on the path of first or second beam. All the features of evolution were explained on basis of interference equations considering orthogonality of linear polarizations of laser modes and change in mode amplitudes and frequencies.

articleTitle: Laser Distance Meter model
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Models of the basic units for laser distance meter are submitted. These models are developed on the basis of an applied package SIMULINK of program system MATLAB.

articleTitle: The optimization of near infrared CW Gd3Ga5O12:Nd-,YAIO3:Nd- AND YVO4:Nd- microlasers
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The modeling of CW GGG:Nd- (1.4237 mum), YAP:Nd- (1.34 mum), YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>:Nd-microlasers (1.0643 mum) is carried out. At that for the each fixed value of the incident pumping power and the laser beam divergence the optimal values of the activator concentration, the active medium length and the reflectivity of the output mirror, i.e. the values that maximize the laser power, are determined.

articleTitle: The temperature distribution and thermomechanical strains in passively Q-switched YAG:Nd3+/YAG:Cr4+ and GGG:Nd3+/GGG:Cr4+ microchip lasers
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The heat processes in microchip Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:YAG- and Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:GGG-lasers passively Q-switched by Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup>:YAG and Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup>:GGG absorbers are considered. The specific heat power is determined from the system of rate equations described the processes of generation/absorption of laser radiation and generation of heat both in the generation medium and the absorber. At known time dependences and space distributions of the specific heat power the distributions of the temperature in both lasers are determined from the heat conduction equation. Based on the distributions of the temperature, the thermo-mechanical strains are estimated. It is shown that maximal values of the thermomechanical strains in GGG-based laser are in ~1.5 times higher than in YAG-based one. Even at the significant heat power the maximal values of the thermo-mechanical strains for both crystals are 4-6 times lower than their limiting values.

articleTitle: Full transparency regime for optical transmission and lasing threshold in silica fibers due to nonlinear Raman interaction
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Raman nonlinearity of single mode fibers is the creation basis of the new class of modern photonic devices such as fiber Raman lasers and fiber Raman amplifiers. The quantitative analysis of the gain start conditions and the Raman laser threshold in the single mode fibers from the point of view the strong gain description of active laser materials will be made in present work. It is shown that the absolute transparency regime for optical transmission in fibers and Raman laser threshold for monochrome signal wave can be directly obtained from standard coupled equations using only fundamental fiber parameters. Limiting condition when material of fiber core starts the transformation from the natural state with attenuation of Stokes wave to the state in which the Stokes wave is amplified due to pump power may be expressed in simple analytical form. The numerical data of laser threshold as function of wavelength and the examples of gain bandwidth determination for several widespread Raman fibers are presented.

articleTitle: Optimization of chirped mirrors
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Refinement of spectral characteristics of chirped mirrors with numerical optimization algorithms is presented. We discuss different forms of merit function. Conjugate gradient method for numerical optimization is used for improvement of single chirped mirrors design as well as chirped mirrorspsila pair. A novel technique based on variation of Bragg wavelength curvature is proposed in order to achieve target phase shift. It allows us to manipulate the dispersion curve of a chirped mirror and particularly half period shift of quasiperiodic GDD resulted in subtraction of GDD oscillations. This is important for designing of complementary chirped mirrorspsila pair.

articleTitle: Numerical calculation of temperature-dependent absorption in end pumped Yb:YAG thin disk laser
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In this paper, the dependence of absorption power on the temperature in an end pumped Yb:YAG quasi-three level thin disk laser is calculated. Here, we have used the temperature-dependent form of Boltzmann occupation factors, absorption cross section and thermal conductivity of the Yb:YAG crystal. A Monte Carlo ray tracing code developed by our group and a 2D finite element analysis (FEA) with the ANSYS package are used to calculate the absorption power and the temperature distribution inside the Yb:YAG thin disk laser respectively. An iterative method used for combination of these two methods to achieve the temperature-dependent absorption power.

articleTitle: Technique of XeCl-excilamps computer modeling
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The procedure of electric-discharge XeCl-excilamps modeling is presented. There are many reports on the different models of XeCl-excilamps, but for practical applications and theoretical analysis having clear physical sense it is useful to consider a general procedure. In general case program of XeCl-excilamps modeling includes the next subprograms: the subprogram for solution of Boltzmann equation for electrons; subprogram for calculation of solving of set of equations for kinetic processes; subprogram for calculation of solving of set of equations for electric circuit of excitation system; data base for cross-section of reaction with electron participation; data base for rate coefficients of reactions with heavy particles, ions and photons participation. The model must be able to calculate an electrons concentration, density of excimer XeCl* molecules and specific energy deposition in active medium. The knowledge of XeCl* molecules concentration has allowed to evaluate the excilamp output power.

articleTitle: Few cycle powerful pulse production under filamention in gaseous media without external compressor
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We present experimental and theoretical investigation of the pulse self compression under femtosecond pulse filamentation in argon cell. It is shown that beam focal length increase and pressure in the cell decrease lead to the better pulse self-compression. Experimental and theoretical results are in good qualitative agreement.

articleTitle: Interaction and fusion of light pulses at the dynamical four-wave mixing in photorefractive media
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: All-optical control of impulse parameters is realized via a dynamical transmission four-wave mixing. We show that the nonlinear system, which includes both coupled wave equations and an evolution equation for the dynamical grating amplitude, contains soliton-like solution for the intensity pattern formed in the medium. The nonlocality of the nonlinear response is the main important requirement to the soliton-like solution is established during the wave-mixing process. On some determined conditions the convergence of input pulses into one pulse takes place (i.e. the merge of the solitons) that lead to the dramatic changes of the output pulse shapes and intensities. The precise conditions, when the impulse output can be driven by another guiding pulse are obtained and discussed.

articleTitle: Resonant two-photon annihilation of an E−-E+ pair in the laser field
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Resonant two photon annihilation of an electron-positron pair in the field of a moderately strong circularly polarized wave is investigated theoretically. There are two pairs of diagrams different by the type of intermediate particle. The kinematics and resonance conditions are found in the case of electron (positron) birth. For moderately strong light wave we derive the expression for the resonant differential cross section of the process. The resonant singularities in the expressions for the amplitude can be eliminated with the use of the Breit-Wigner procedure.

articleTitle: Formation of a beam with a uniform intensity distribution of radiation in a waveguide rectangular resonator with a nonuniform mirror
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The method of obtaining of wave beams with a uniform intensity profile in the waveguide quasioptical resonator (WQR) is described. It is based on the self-imaging properties of multimode rectangular waveguides and using the nonuniform mirror with the discretely distributed absorbing or scattering sections. The theoretical model and calculation algorithm of characteristics of the low-loss Fourier-mode with uniform intensity distribution at the output mirror of the WQR are developed with application of the eigenmodes and the Fourier-optics methods. The conditions of Fourier-mode existence are established by changing the resonator geometry and its nonuniform mirror parameters.

articleTitle: Modeling of a vertical cavity surface emitting laser containing a resonant multi-QW heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: A vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) containing a resonant heterostructure of an array of quantum wells (QW) is considered. The set of QW separated by barriers represents a periodical structure with period equal to a laser wavelength. Bragg reflectors serve as the laser mirrors. In the first stage we study ldquocoldrdquo cavity properties neglecting change of material characteristics induced by the electromagnetic field. The eigenvalue problem to determine the resonator modes is solved numerically. Complex eigenvalues found define the wavelength shifts relative to reference value and threshold gains. The next stage of study relates to a case of a loaded cavity when self-consistent solving of a wave field equation and material equations is required. The charge carrier distributions in each of QW obey non-linear diffusion equation. We have developed the special iteration procedure for round-trip operator evaluation, which is applicable for a set of QW of any size and has computational costs growing linearly with number of QW. The results of calculations for a cylindrical VCSEL with e-beam pumping will be reported.

articleTitle: Non-traditional structures of interferometer Fabry-Perot for IR spectral region
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The analytic expressions that allow calculate the optimal parameters of dielectrics layers and parameters of metallic film in structures ldquodielectric layer - metallic film - dielectrics layerrdquo and the analytic expressions for the analysis structure ldquodielectric layer - interference mirror - dielectric layerrdquo are obtained.

articleTitle: Analysis of wave structure functions
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Wave structure function (WSF) of spherical wave is used in extended Huygens-Fresnel integral to induce the effect of turbulent atmosphere on the propagating laser beam. Depending on the approximation made and the choice of the spatial power spectral density of refractive index fluctuation function, different forms of WSFs become available. In this study, five different WSFs are numerically evaluated for pure Gaussian, cosh-Gaussian, sinh-Gaussian, cos-Gaussian and sine-Gaussian types of source plane beams. In the range of adapted source and propagation parameters, namely under weak fluctuation conditions, no substantial deviations are found to occur with respect to the WSF selection. Our results are offered in terms of graphical illustrations showing the differences in the receiver intensity profiles against the varying propagation distance.

articleTitle: A new binary multi-layer diffraction grating
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In WDM communication systems, diffraction grating is an important component. Optical components such as multiplexers use diffraction grating in their structures. In these devices, a grating with good specification (high angular dispersion, high diffraction efficiency, and low polarization dependence) is strongly desired. Since reducing the reflection at the upper surface of a grating is an important issue in order to realize high optical performance, we propose a novel grating with multi-layer structure in which a thin layer is used for decreasing the reflection from the surface. A good design, which provides high optical performance in the broad wavelength band, is successfully obtained.

articleTitle: Anisotropic photonic crystals and microcavities based on dispersive anisotropic porous silicon
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The model for description of one-dimensional anisotropic photonic crystals and microcavities based on dispersive anisotropic porous silicon is proposed. The finite difference technique is applied for the scattering matrix parameter computation. Reflectance spectra for two orthogonal polarizations of the incident plane wave are calculated.

articleTitle: Modeling and numerical analysis of temperature variations along the cavity and in the heat sink of a single quantum well high power laser diode
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In this paper, thermal behavior of GaAs/AlGaAs single quantum well (SQW) high power laser diode (HPLD) is modeled by means of finite difference method (FDM). A numerical model is introduced that calculates the time dependant axial variations of photon density, carrier density and temperature in the semiconductor laser, self-consistently. The dynamic response of the high power laserpsilas back facet temperature and the influence of the surface recombination velocity on the temperature of both facets are modeled numerically. The two-dimensional temperature distribution in the Cupper heat sink is also demonstrated. In order to gain precise results we use the Fermipsilas Golden Rule to calculate the exact temperature-dependent gain function of the quantum well laser.

articleTitle: Change of photon polarization in magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The process of photon propagation in external strong magnetic field has been studied. Resonance conditions in approximation of strong magnetic field and weakly excited electron (positron) states have been found. The process probability as a function of polarization parameters has been obtained. In resonance the polarization of the final photon practically does not depend on the polarization of initial photon. Final photon has linear polarization in the plane of wave vector and magnetic field.

articleTitle: Generation of clusters of optical vortices
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We demonstrate that the regular ring-shaped arrays of Gaussian beams, or optical clusters, can be generated using diffraction on a stack of dielectric wedges.

articleTitle: The peculiarity on radiation spectrum of the system of four electrons moving in a spiral in transparent medium
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The fine structure for the spectral distribution of the time-averaged radiation power of four electrons moving one by one along a spiral in transparent medium in relativistic case is studied by using the analytical and numerical methods. Special attention is given to the research of the spectral distribution of radiation power of four electrons in dependence of the magnitude of time shifts between the electrons.

articleTitle: Laser action in photonic crystal structures with activated glass
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We present the theoretical and numerical approach to the computation of the lasing from 1D and 2D photonic crystal structures with active medium for nonlinear case. We used the transfer matrix formalism for studying the amplification in a photonic crystal. The lazing optimum condition is determined. The parameters of photonic crystal laser based on activated glasses can choose by this method.

articleTitle: Demonstration of interference and laser generation instabilities in semiconductor laser beam reflected from glass plate
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: A simple scheme of two-beam interference is presented in the work. It includes glass plate of thickness 1-2 mm and laser beam focused on it (focusing by a collecting lens with focal distance of about 10 cm). Observations of interference in reflected light were conducted at a remote screen placed at distance of several meters away. The formula for interference pattern period has been deduced for such a case. It has been shown that the scheme is good for educational demonstrations of interference. Besides, it has been shown that, provided the light source is a semiconductor laser with unstable generation spectrum, generation instability is revealed through interference pattern observations. Thus a simple but high-quality method of detecting laser generation instabilities is proposed.

articleTitle: Nonresonance spontaneous bremsstrahlung of an electron scattered by a nucleus in a pulsed light field
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The paper presents a theoretical study of nonresonance spontaneous bremsstrahlung of an electron scattered by a nucleus in the field of a pulsed light wave. The approximation is considered when a pulsewidth is considerably large than the characteristic time of the wave oscillation. The analytical expressions for the amplitude and cross-section of nonresonance spontaneous bremsstrahlung of an electron scattered by a nucleus in the moderate pulsed light field are derived. It is concluded, that for process spontaneous bremsstrahlung of an electron scattered by a nucleus in the field of pulsed light wave the distribution of stimulated emission (absorption) probability over the number of wave photons has the significant shift to small values relatively corresponding distribution in the case monochromatic wave.

articleTitle: Influence of the electron-ion recombination on the positive column characteristics in narrow discharge tubes
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The theoretical analysis of the influence of a volume electron-ionic recombination on energy and spatial characteristics of discharge plasma of positive column in narrow gas-discharge tube is developed. It is shown that under some conditions even in a diffusion mode of glow discharge this influence reduces to essential modifications of interior gas discharge parameters. The basic equations are: the equation of energy balance (in local approximation) of electrons in positive column for determination the intensity of the longitudinal electric field, the balance equation of the number of charged particles and the equation for the discharge current. The interior parameters of discharge plasma (electronic temperature and electron concentration on an axis) experience variations caused by transition of glow discharge from diffusion mode to volume at increase of gas pressure and discharge current. The numerical calculations for the discharge in helium are carried out.

articleTitle: Simulation of intramolecular dynamics at transformation of two light pulses by molecules of active media of photochemical lasers
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Using a numerical solution of a system of equations for matrix elements of file-level model molecule density operator time dependencies of population on its states at different values of two irradiation pulses parameters (the pump pulse and the dump (or probe) pulse) and constants, determining rates of induced radiative transitions of the molecule, and radiative and nonradiative decays of the molecular states are calculated. The values of these constants were taken, in particular, close to these of the corresponding constants of molecules with intramolecular hydrogen bond as the 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) molecule. Values of irradiation pulses parameters are obtained, at which after enol-keto photoisomerization, induced by pump pulse, dump pulse induces molecular transition from excited electronic state in keto-form to ground state in this (ldquotautomericrdquo) form. This transition is accompanied by stimulated emission with a frequency of ldquotautomericrdquo fluorescence. Examples of periodic change of intensity of the stimulated emission are given, the frequency of oscillations of fluorescence intensity being proportional to dump pulse intensity.

articleTitle: Nonresonant electron-muon scattering in the pulsed electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The nonresonant scattering of an electron by a muon in the field of a pulsed light wave in the frame of the Born approximation is investigated theoretically. The approximation when a pulsewidth is considerably greater than the characteristic time of the wave oscillation is considered. The analytical expressions for the amplitude and cross-section of mentioned process are derived in case of moderately strong elliptically polarized wave. It is shown that in the case of initial particlespsila relativistic energies the partial differential cross-section is factorized as a product of the cross-section of electron-muon scattering in the absence of the external field and the probability of emission (absorption) |l| photons from the wave. After summation over all possible processes of wave photons emission and absorption all the essential quantum terms cancel each other. As a result the cross-section coincides with the cross-section of electron-muon scattering in the absence of the external field.

articleTitle: Calculation of dynamic characteristics of thin-film optical filters
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The principles of transient calculation of multilayer thin-film optical filters with Monte-Carlo method application are considered. This method allows taking into account the influence of a multiple reflection of light quantums in thin-film structures.

articleTitle: Optical coupling of two microcavities with time discontinuity in permittivity
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The paper is devoted to the theoretical study of the optical coupling by whispering gallery modes (WGM) in a double-cavity photonic molecule (PM) and the sensitivity of such coupling to the time material variation of individual resonator. A semi-analytical solution is obtained for the case of instantaneous change of dielectric permittivity. The possibility of frequency shifting is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Gaussian beam scattering from a bi-isotropic photonic structure
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The three-dimensional Gaussian beam scattering from the bounded periodic sequence of one-to-one composed isotropic magnetodielectric and bi-isotropic layers are investigated. The beam field is represented by an angular continuous spectrum of plane wave. The problem of the partial plane wave diffraction on the structure is solved using the circuit theory and the transfer matrix methods. It is found that after reflection from the structure, the circular Gaussian beam becomes, in general, an elliptical Gaussian beam, in addition to a displacement of the beam axis from the position predicted by ray optics.

articleTitle: The cores of waveguide structure in waist of fused biconical tapered coupler
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The work presents the results of investigation of wave-guide structures of fused biconical tapered couplers fabricated from single-mode quartz fibers with various GeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> concentrations in the cores. It has been demonstrated that the cross-section dimensions differ in the coupler waists. The authors assume that the experimentally observed dependence of the wave-guide-to-wave-guide coupling in the coupler waist on the fusion mode is determined by a change of the cross-section areas ratio of the cores.

articleTitle: Wide modal gain spectra in the asymmetric multiple-quantum-well heterostructures Ga0.47In0.53As-Ga0.18In0.82As0.4P0.6
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: For asymmetric multiple-quantum-well heterostructures based on Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>As-Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.18</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.82</sub>As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub> compounds, the detailed theoretical analysis of modal gain spectra is carried out in the framework of the four-band kp-method. Effective procedure of obtaining the wide and practically flat modal gain spectrum is offered. Various designs of the semiconductor sources with different sets of non-uniform excited quantum wells, giving a wide gain spectrum in the 1.28-1.6 mum ranges, are calculated.

articleTitle: Interchannel soliton collisions in periodic dispersion maps in the presence of third order dispersion with loss and amplification
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We study the effects of third-order dispersion in wavelength division multiplexed soliton transmission systems using periodic dispersion maps. For this purpose, loss and lumped amplification have been included in a previous ODE model obtained using the variational method and a Gaussian ansatz. We present a detailed analysis of how TOD affects the collision-induced frequency shifts of the transmitted pulses.

articleTitle: One-photon annihilation of an electron-positron pair in the intense pulsed laser field
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We theoretically investigate one-photon annihilation of an electron-positron pair in the intense pulsed laser field. It is demonstrated that a process of one-photon annihilation is possible only with emission of a large number of the wave photons within the range of the optical frequencies of a laser field. Itpsilas shown that a probability of the one-photon annihilation is optimal for the intense laser field.

articleTitle: Properties of fluoride materials and coatings for various optical systems
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Properties of low-refractive-index materials based on fluorides of metals, presumably, complex ones, and coatings produced from them, are regarded. Problems of optimization of composition of film-forming materials, based on fluorides, by their alloying are discussed. An alloying mechanism of admixtures to the most widespread material-magnesium fluoride-is established. Another way of enhancing optical properties, particularly, broadening of a transparency domain due to use of complex fluorides is shown. High beam durability and transparency of BaY<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> allow regarding it as much promising material for interference optics of IR technological lasers.

articleTitle: Analysis and comparison of multiwavelength Raman amplifiers with different configurations
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We analyze the performances and characteristics of multiwavelength Raman amplifiers that are designed in backward or bi-directional pumping which can be used in dispersion compensator and low noise amplifiers and compare several configurations of a Raman amplifier system. The results show that amplitude spontaneous emission (ASE) in backward pumping is less than bi-directional pumping with improved noise figure. In addition, for backward and bi-directional pumping the system ability can be better by appropriate design of pump powers and wavelengths of system.

articleTitle: Random lasing under diffusive light propogation
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The physical model of random lasing (RL) based on the concept of feedback distributed laser (FDL) are developed. It based on similarity of RL formation from scattered waves in a random laser and from reflected waves in FDL. In contrast to FDL the RL spatial feedback distribution along the radiation trajectories is random. All radiation trajectories interrelated in the tangle by scattering can be represented as the imaginary one-dimensional chain including all enabled scatterers and keeping radiation under any scattering event. Output intensity of this chain is described by the expression being similar to one for the single-pass amplifier with length determined by concentration of scattering particles and gain. The expression adequately describes the main RL behaviors: narrowing of radiation spectrum under pump intensity and scatterer concentration increase.

articleTitle: Alternative methods for antireflection of optical surfaces with use of the transition layers and diffraction gratings
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The new methods for antireflection of optical surfaces with use of the transition layers and diffraction gratings, is researched. The optimal profile of refractive index variation for transition layer is determined. For antireflection of the boundary ldquotransparent dielectric-airrdquo the relief diffraction grating is shaped on surface of dielectric. The profiles of grating groove that minimize of reflectance, is searched.

articleTitle: Semi-analytical semiconductor parameters extraction algorithm for optical link simulations
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In this paper, we present a simple algorithm for extraction of laser rate equation parameters based on a set of simple laboratory measurements. Commercial semiconductor DFB laser (Fujitsu FLD3F7CZ) with central wavelength 1310 nm is used to obtain the P-I and frequency response curves. Simulation results using the extracted parameters are in good agreement with the experimental results in both small and large signal modulation.

articleTitle: Modeling of end-pumped CW Yb:YAG disk laser
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: A new model has been developed to describe behaviour of disk lasers. We have derived analytic expressions from a set of coupled rate equations which include the effects of the pump and the laser states simultaneously in order to investigate the influence of the effective parameters on the operational efficiency of a high gain, end-pumped quasi-three-level Yb:YAG disk laser. Based upon our results, we have examined laser output power as a function of thickness and doping concentration of the disk, number of pump beam passes, and absorbed pump power.

articleTitle: Polarizable vacuum approach for describing of gravitation induced optical effects
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The Maxwell equations with accounting for tensors properties of time have been considered. It has been demonstrated that introduction of the time tensor enables describing the changes in the velocities of electromagnetic waves in the so-called polarized vacuum, as well as anisotropy of those velocities. We have analyzed the propagation of light near a electrically charged, static spherical mass. The relations that describe the changes in the refractive index, dielectric impermeability and polarizability of vacuum under the influence of gravitation and electrical fields have been derived. One can see that vacuum possess polarizability and last is equal zero only at anyone field absence that is impossible in reality. Hence we have good reasons to conclude: vacuum is polarizable medium.

articleTitle: Change of spectrum width of tunable ultrashort pulses of radiation of distributed feedback dye laser
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The spectrum width of ultrashort light pulses produced by a distributed feedback dye laser (DFDL) is numerically investigated depending on lasing wavelength. It is established that the spectrum width broadening taking place in the course of wavelength tuning is caused by the appropriate change of the emission and absorption cross sections of dye molecules.

articleTitle: Enhanced passively Q-switched Nd:YAG lasers modeling
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In this paper, a modified model that accurately predicts the dynamic behaviour of passively Q-switched solid-state lasers is introduced. The proposed simulation model can be used for predicting the design parameters of passively Q-switched Nd:YAG lasers using Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup>:YAG crystal as saturable absorber. Simulation results using the proposed enhanced model are in good agreement with the experimental and published results of commercial / lab realized systems.

articleTitle: Polarization and spin effects in processes of synchrotron radiation and pair creation in strong magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The photon-induced process of electron-positron pair creation in a strong homogeneous magnetic field, provided that the polarization of particles is arbitrary, has been considered. The polarization of a photon is described in terms of the well-known Stokes parameters, and the relevant probabilities of the process turn out to have simple analytical expressions, which allows us to analyze the polarization and spin effects. A substantial influence of the linear polarization of a photon on the spin orientations of electrons and positrons has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Methods of computer modeling of uniform field laser electrodes profile
publicationTitle: 2008 9th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The procedure of electric-discharge laser electrodes profile modeling, using MathCad, is presented. There are sufficiently many reports on the modeling of uniform field electrodes profile, but for practical applications it is useful to consider a general procedure. Three types of profiles are widely used for profiling electrodes for gas discharges used for CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and excimer lasers. These are Rogowski profile, Chang profile, and Ernst profile. The properties of original profile are discussed.
